question.text: An organic compound '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>' contains nitrogen and chlorine. It dissolves readily in water to give a solution that turns litmus red. Titration of compound '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>' with standard base indicates that the molecular weight of '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>' is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>131</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. When a sample of '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>' is treated with aq. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>NaOH</mi></math>, a liquid separates which contains <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> but not <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Cl</mi></math>. Treatment of the obtained liquid with nitrous acid followed by phenol gives orange precipitate. The compound '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>' is

solution.text: Anilinium chloride is acidic in solution and turns blue litmus red. With Nitrous acid, it forms benzendiazonium chloride. Which reacts with phenol in alkaline medium gives orange coloured solution where the reaction follows electrophilic substitution reaction and the electrophile is benzene diazonium ion
